newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says US helped reduce militant danger.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says US helped reduce militant danger.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday Washington had helped Israel reduce the danger of militant attacks against the Jewish state.
"I can say that the United States helped us and -- at my request and initiation -- aided us in a meaningful way in order to lessen the danger of terror," Netanyahu said.
"The danger of mass terrorist attacks has not passed," he added. He did not elaborate on the kind of help provided by the United States in curbing militant attacks.
Netanyahu's comments were excerpted from an interview to appear later on Tuesday on Israel Channel Two television and broadcast on Israel's army radio.
On Monday, Israeli media said Netanyahu had sent messages to Syria through the United States and to Iran through Germany demanding they prevent the militant Islamic Jihad group from attacking Israel.
Netanyahu's spokesman said he could not comment on the reports.

Israeli security sources said on Sunday there was information a guerrilla squad was in Israel to avenge the October 26, 1995, assassination in Malta of Islamic Jihad leader Fathi Shqaqi. His killers were not captured and Palestinians blamed Israel.
The Jewish state went on high alert deploying security forces and setting up roadblocks in crowded areas. The measures were eased on Monday but the alert remained.

Netanyahu, asked if tensions had lessened on Tuesday because there had been arrests or if he could say with certainty that an attack had been foiled, replied: "I don't think that in this area (the fight against militants) anything is certain."
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Tuesday that the security alert was still in force.
"The warning was serious and we think that today it is still serious...This is the principal reason we have still not opened the closure on the (Arab) territories," Mordechai said on army radio.
Israel on October 23 sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, barring Palestinians from going to work in the Jewish state, for fear of Islamic Jihad attacks.

Islamic Jihad and Hamas leaders in areas under Palestinian Authority rule have been in jail since suicide bombings in February and March, responsibility for which was claimed by Hamas, the other leading Islamic resistance group in Palestinian areas. Those attacks killed 59 people.
